newsitem.title: USA: Airgas March 31 Q4 to include charge.
newsitem.headline: Airgas March 31 Q4 to include charge.

text.p: Gas distributor Airgas Inc said Monday results for the fourth-quarter ended March 31 will include a non-recurring charge from damages incurred from an allegedly fraudulent breach of a contract by a third-party supplier, among other things.
The company said a writedown related to two non-core, product-line businesses, and a loss related to the sale of a Canadian medical home-care business will also contribute to the charge.
It said it will take a non-recurring pre-tax charge of about $26 million for the allegedly fraudulent breach of contract by a third-party supplier of refrigerant gas.
"We expect the loss from the fraudulent breach of contract to be partially offset by insurance claims along with cash and inventories recovered in litigation," it said.

The company said it will take a pre-tax, non-cash charge of about $5 million for the writedown of certain machinery and equipment, goodwill and other intangible assets of two non-core, product-line businesses.
It said it had recognized a $700,000 after-tax loss on the sale of a medical home-care business in Ontario.

"Although our after-tax cash flow for the quarter is expected to show solid growth, our earnings per share, excluding the refrigerant and other charges and the loss associated with the sale of our Ontario medical home-care business, are expected to be slightly below the $0.17 per share reported in the fourth quarter of our 1996 fiscal year," it said.
First Call's consensus among industry analysts had been for earnings of $0.19 a share for the period.

Airgas, a distributor of industrial, medical and specialty gases and related equipment in North America with annual sales in excess of $1.2 billion, expects to report its results for the fourth quarter and full 1997 fiscal year on May 8.
